page.title: Help
page.subtitle: Usage articles for the five pages, plus “?” notes in the UI

workbench.title: Workbench
workbench.desc: Create and import templates, organize them by group

designer.title: Designer
designer.desc: Design label layouts on the canvas

data.title: Data & Print
data.desc: Fill in data and print, with Excel batch support

jobs.title: Job History
jobs.desc: Browse print records and per-label details

settings.title: Settings
settings.desc: Language, server address, printer and plugin settings on this machine

workbench.intro: The workbench is where templates start: create a blank template, or import a previously exported template file; as the list grows, search and group filter help you locate them quickly.

designer.intro: The designer edits label layouts: place elements from the widget bar, arrange them on the canvas, and tune them in the properties panel — the “?” beside each group explains every setting. The “Print Fields” and “Layers” lists on the left update automatically as you design, and the “Test Defaults” tab manages the values used for test prints.

data.intro: Data & Print turns a template into labels: pick a template, fill in data, choose a target device and print. Check the result first with “Image Preview” or “Simulate output”; Excel batching and job progress are covered below, and full records live in Job History.

jobs.intro: Job History is where you review print results; list refresh, per-label details and copying job IDs are covered in the sections below. Server-side records are kept for 30 days by default and cleaned up on expiry; records stored on this machine are kept.

settings.intro: Settings gathers this machine's configuration: interface language, server address, connection, print batching, printer, updates & packages, and plugin management; the “?” beside each card title explains that item.

cards.title: Template Cards & Thumbnails
cards.body: Template cards show the name, group and a thumbnail preview rendered with sample data; click the thumbnail to enlarge it. Double-click the card to open the designer.

actions.title: Card Actions
actions.body:
Use “Edit” on the card, or “Print” to fill in data and print this template in Data & Print. 
The “⋯” menu holds export and delete: export produces a template file you can import again later; delete asks for confirmation and cannot be undone.

filter.title: Search & Group Filter
filter.body: The search box filters by template name (case-insensitive) and the dropdown filters by group; both apply together, so when nothing matches, check the keyword and the group.

canvas.title: Canvas & Widget Bar
canvas.body:
Place text, barcodes, QR codes and rectangles from the widget bar; drag to arrange, helped by smart guides and the millimeter grid. 
Shortcuts: Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+C/V copy & paste, Delete remove, middle-drag pan, Ctrl+wheel zoom. 
“Preview Print” shows the label at true print scale for the selected “Print DPI” (dots per inch, set in the top toolbar); the canvas locks while previewing — exit to keep editing.

fieldsSide.title: Print Fields & Layers
fieldsSide.body:
Print fields are derived automatically: any element whose source is “Field fill” counts as a field — no manual registration needed. 
The layer list orders elements back to front; click to select, use To Top / Up / Down / To Bottom to restack, Delete to remove.

testData.title: Test Defaults
testData.body: Test defaults are generated from element preview values: set a preview value on a “Field fill” widget, save the template, and it becomes the default for test prints (PC and PDA).

saveFlow.title: Save & Leave Guard
saveFlow.body:
“Save Template” writes the current layout; saving a new or renamed template that already exists asks for overwrite confirmation. 
Leaving with unsaved changes offers save & leave, discard, or stay.

position.title: Position / Size
position.body: X / Y position the element relative to the label content area; width and height are in millimeters (mm), minimum 1. Lines have no width or height; they use Length X / Length Y instead.

fill.title: Fill: Fixed Value or Field
fill.body:
“Source” decides what prints: “Fixed value” renders the text as entered, for content that never changes; “Field fill” swaps in external data at print time. 
The field name is what the data is matched by — name it location, and printing takes the location value from your data. “Display name” only affects the print page and falls back to the field name when empty; the preview value shows on the canvas only and is ignored at print time.

box.title: Border / Padding
box.body: Applies to text, barcode and QR code elements: left/right and top/bottom padding pull content inward, and the border draws along the element edge. All values are millimeters, minimum 0; defaults are fine in most cases.

text.title: Text / Font
text.body: “Font”, “Font height”, “Line spacing” and the alignment options control typography. With “Wrap” on, text that is too wide wraps to the next line, and anything past the bottom edge is not shown; with it off, text stays on one line and the overflow follows the “Single-line overflow” setting — “Shrink to fit” scales the line down until it fits, “Hide” cuts off the excess. Bold prints more clearly, especially at small font heights.

barcode.title: Barcode Parameters
barcode.body:
“Symbology” is the barcode type: Code128 handles letters and digits and fits most cases; EAN13 is the 13-digit retail code; UPC is the 12-digit North American retail code; CODE39 is common in industry and logistics. 
“Show text below” toggles the human-readable line under the bars. “Module width” is the width of the narrowest bar — smaller packs the bars tighter; if scanners struggle, increase it.

qrcode.title: QR Code Parameters
qrcode.body:
Error correction L / M / Q / H recovers roughly 7% / 15% / 25% / 30%: higher survives more damage but carries less data; M fits most cases. 
Margin adds quiet space around the code (mm). Width and height are linked; change one and the other follows.

rect.title: Rectangle
rect.body: Rectangles are hollow: only the border is drawn, with no fill — handy for dividing up a label or drawing table grid lines. Border thickness is in millimeters.

line.title: Line
line.body:
Lines cannot be created from the widget bar; they usually come in with imported designs and still display and print correctly. 
Length X / Length Y set horizontal, vertical or slanted lines; thickness is in millimeters (minimum 0.1). Rectangle borders also work for table grid lines.

compat.title: Image / Container
compat.body: Images and containers likewise cannot be created from the widget bar — they arrive with imported designs and travel with template package import/export. A container frames a group of elements and only shows its Id here (read-only); images cannot be edited on this page; both can adjust their border.

align.title: Align
align.body: Appears with 2 or more elements selected: align left / center / right or top / middle / bottom, using the bounding box as reference. Containers don't participate.

form.title: Template & Data Entry
form.body: Pick a template on the left, then fill its fields; a static label (no field fills) prints as-is with no data. “Target device” chooses the online device that executes the print; if this machine isn't joined to the server, printing falls back to local.

debug.title: Image Preview & Simulated Print
debug.body:
“Image Preview” shows the current label in an in-page overlay and can download it; “Simulate output” renders at the exact resolution of a real print, supports whole batches, prints nothing and creates no record — use it to verify the final result. 
Unlike “Simulated printing” in Settings (a printer connection mode that saves jobs as image files), it works right on this page.

excel.title: Excel Batch Printing
excel.body:
“Download Excel Template” builds a sheet from the current template's fields (sample row included), one row per label. 
“Import Excel” then asks you to confirm which column maps to which field (auto-matched by column name, adjustable); unmapped columns don't print. Then submit the batch job.

progress.title: Job Progress & Retry
progress.body: After submitting, the Job Progress panel tracks completed labels and per-label results; failed ones can be retried one by one from the list. Failure reasons are kept in Job History; expand the job there to see them.

overview.title: List & Refresh
overview.body: The list shows the last 100 print records: job ID, target device and a completed / failed summary. It refreshes automatically while a job is running; the reload button refreshes on demand.

detail.title: Details & Copy Job ID
detail.body: Click a row to expand its per-label details (local direct-print jobs only; server-dispatched jobs show a summary), including each label's failure reason. Click the job ID to copy the full ID for feedback and troubleshooting.

language.title: Language
language.body: Switching takes effect immediately and is saved in this browser; the first launch follows the browser language.

serverAddress.title: Server Address
serverAddress.body:
The server stores all templates and print records; the address is normally configured by the installer. Confirm with your administrator before changing it. 
Run “Test Connection”, then “Save and Apply”; the saved address persists across restarts. Without a server you can still print directly on this machine (standalone mode).

transport.title: Connection
transport.body:
The card collapses to the current connection; expand it to test or switch the printer connection. Switching happens only after “Test Connection” passes; on failure the reason is shown and the current connection is kept. The saved connection is used after restart. 
“Simulated printing” needs no printer: labels are generated as images saved on this machine, handy for checking the result first.

batch.title: Print Batching
batch.body: When enabled, large jobs are sent to the printer in batches of the configured “Labels per batch”, with the configured “Batch interval” between batches to ease the strain of continuous printing. Changes take effect immediately after saving.

printer.title: Printer
printer.body: The card shows the printer's current status (paper out, paused, and so on). “Test Print” sends one test page (a test barcode) to the connected printer; check for paper afterwards.

updates.title: Updates & Packages
updates.body:
Packages are distributed by the server: the card compares the local version with the latest; download a package from the list and run it to upgrade (the client does not upgrade itself), or ask your administrator for help. 
In standalone mode no packages are listed; connect to a server under “Server Address” above first.

plugins.title: Plugin Management
plugins.body: “Server plugins” lists what can be installed; “Installed Plugins” lists what is on this machine. Install from the list above, or uninstall what is no longer needed — either way, restart the client for changes to take effect. Nothing is listed in standalone mode.

demo.active: Showing sample data; exiting restores your previous values; nothing is saved.

deepLink.timeout: Page switched; if no topic appears, open a template and select an element, then click “?”.
deepLink.draftOpened: The sample draft opened from Help is temporary: it is discarded when you leave and nothing is saved automatically.
